board_content.text: When are two complex numbers equal?
Two addresses match only if BOTH coordinates agree.
Satisfying only one equation is the partial-equality error.
One complex equation therefore becomes TWO real equations.
Standard Method B: for $A+iB=C+iD$ in real unknowns, set $A=C$ and $B=D$.
You then solve the two simultaneous real equations for the real unknowns.
Match real-to-real and imaginary-to-imaginary — never mix them.

segments_english.text: When do we say two complex numbers are equal? This looks trivial but it hides the single most-tested technique of the subtopic.
a plus i b equals c plus i d if and only if a equals c and b equals d. Both conditions, joined by and, are required.
Go back to the address analogy: two addresses name the same place only when both the east coordinate and the north coordinate agree. One matching coordinate is not enough.
That's exactly where students lose marks: they satisfy only the real part or only the imaginary part. That's the partial-equality error, and it's an easy trap to fall into under time pressure.
The upside is powerful: a single complex equation quietly hands you two real equations for free.
This is Standard Method B. Given some expression A plus i B equals C plus i D in real unknowns, you set A equal to C, and separately B equal to D.
Now you have two ordinary simultaneous real equations, and you solve them for your real unknowns like any system from earlier algebra.
Just remember the discipline: match real part to real part, and imaginary part to imaginary part. Never let a real term equal an imaginary term.

segments_hinglish.text: Do complex numbers ko equal kab kehte hain? Ye trivial lagta hai par isme subtopic ki sabse zyada test hone wali technique chhupi hai.
a plus i b equals c plus i d if and only if a equals c aur b equals d. Dono conditions, and se judi, zaroori hain.
Address analogy par wapas: do addresses ek hi jagah ko tabhi naam dete hain jab east coordinate aur north coordinate dono match karein. Ek coordinate match karna kaafi nahi.
Yehi wo jagah hai jahan students marks khote hain: wo sirf real part ya sirf imaginary part satisfy karte hain. Ye partial-equality error hai, aur time pressure mein aasani se ho jaata hai.
Faayda powerful hai: ek single complex equation chupke se aapko do real equations muft mein de deti hai.
Ye hai Standard Method B. Kisi expression A plus i B equals C plus i D mein, real unknowns ke saath, aap A ko C ke barabar, aur alag se B ko D ke barabar set karo.
Ab aapke paas do ordinary simultaneous real equations hain, aur unhe apne real unknowns ke liye solve karo, jaise koi bhi purana algebra system.
Bas discipline yaad rakho: real part ko real part se, aur imaginary part ko imaginary part se match karo. Kabhi real term ko imaginary term ke barabar mat karo.
